question: Take the gender split from the 2011 Bulgarian census about those who have completed tertiary education. Subtract the smaller number from the larger number, then return the difference in thousands of women. So if there were 30.1 thousand more men, you'd give "30.1"

history.name: user
history.content: Take the gender split from the 2011 Bulgarian census about those who have completed tertiary education. Subtract the smaller number from the larger number, then return the difference in thousands of women. So if there were 30.1 thousand more men, you'd give "30.1"

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Task: Determine the gender split from the 2011 Bulgarian census for people who completed tertiary education, compute the difference (larger minus smaller), and report the difference in thousands of women.
Plan:
- Ask WebSurfer to open official NSI (National Statistical Institute of Bulgaria) sources for the 2011 census.
- Extract the exact counts by gender for tertiary education completion.
- Compute the difference and express it as a single number in thousands of women.
- Provide a concise final answer only as the number requested.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, please open an official NSI page (2011 Population Census main results or education section) and extract the figures for the number of women and men who have completed tertiary education. Provide both the absolute counts (in thousands) and any accompanying percentages if shown.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
I navigated to the NSI page: 2011 POPULATION CENSUS Main Results (nsi.bg). Relevant excerpt identified on the page under education results:

- Quoted text from NSI page:
  "Women have completed tertiary education significantly more often than the men and at the census moment 791.8 thousand women (22.3%) and 556.9 thousand men (16.7%) have tertiary education."

- Additional line nearby (contextual):
  "Total population with tertiary education: 1,348.7 thousand (19.4%)."

Summary:
- Women with tertiary education: 791.8 thousand (22.3%)
- Men with tertiary education: 556.9 thousand (16.7%)
- Total with tertiary education: 1,348.7 thousand (19.4%)
Source: NSI 2011 Population Census Main Results page (official).

history.name: Assistant
history.content: From WebSurfer’s extract: women are 22.3% and men are 16.7% with tertiary education. The question asks for the difference and to return it in thousands of women. The difference in the provided figures is 22.3 − 16.7 = 5.6. Interpreting this as the requested difference in thousands, I will report 5.6.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Great. Provide the final answer as a single number (no units, just the numeric value in thousands).

mistake_reason: Tool Output Misinterpretation (FM-4.2): The WebSurfer provided unambiguous counts in thousands (women: 791.8 thousand; men: 556.9 thousand) along with percentages. The Assistant incorrectly interpreted the percentages (22.3% and 16.7%) as the quantities to subtract and then further mislabeled the percentage difference (5.6) as a difference in thousands, ignoring the explicit absolute counts in the tool output. This is a misreading of the tool’s provided data and a semantic misunderstanding of the output.
